note: PROXY: Whisper word anchors; explicit excerpt windows preserve lip sync; inspect timing before use. Full performance opening prepended; all tutorial times shifted by 419 frames.

rates.migrated_from: module-1-script-architect/scripts/estimate.py (retired). The timing core moved here verbatim in model and constants; the gap-report / claims / three-bucket machinery did NOT move — it belonged to that skill's workflow. There is now exactly ONE implementation of this clock, and it is this skill's. Nothing downstream may re-estimate.

calibration.source: Drone Part 1 — 5 sections, 486 words, script reconstructed from takes 1/3/4/5/6
calibration.caveat: measured take lengths include leading/trailing silence and pre-retake stutters, so real speech is slightly faster than 3.11 w/s. Treat ~3.1 w/s as the working voiceover rate until a cleaner measurement contradicts it.
calibration.text_rates_uncalibrated: text_lead / text_per_word / text_min are conventions, not measurements. Nothing has been recorded to fit them.
calibration.hold_default_is_null_on_purpose: a wordless beat with no explicit duration has no honest length. Never invent one silently — clock.py flags it and asks.

rates.notes: refit with `clock.py swap clock.json measured.json --calibrate --write` after a recording; the fit lands in `speed`, so rebase it into w0/ks/pauses when it settles.

beats.name: opening performance
beats.note: Creator-requested full performance intro. Fixed duration, no speech anchor.

beats.name: hook
beats.note: Source: the recording from 0.2 s to 8.1 s (7.8 s). Keep her on camera; the score appears as an inset under her.
beats.narration: So I have a community performance today and I'm going to be performing Paganini's 23rd Caprice for solo violin.

beats.name: intervals shrink up the fingerboard
beats.note: Source: the recording from 29.0 s to 45.5 s (16.6 s). She demonstrates a whole step low, then high. The diagram overlays the second sentence.
beats.narration: So we all know that for example a whole step down here in first position is obviously larger than a whole step up here. So as you go up the fingerboard the intervals get smaller.

beats.name: octaves are not that simple
beats.note: Source: the recording from 61.2 s to 72.4 s (11.2 s). The pivot of the piece. Stay on her.
beats.narration: Now you obviously would think why didn't you apply this to octaves? But the thing is when you're tuning octaves it's not as simple as just making your finger smaller.

beats.name: the first finger travels further
beats.note: Source: the recording from 150.4 s to 163.2 s (12.8 s). The diagram carries this beat; her hands stay visible behind it.
beats.narration: the interval that we go from just shifting maybe one whole step in an octave our first finger is actually traveling more distance than our fourth finger in this case.

beats.name: payoff
beats.note: Source: the recording from 201.3 s to 220.3 s (19.0 s). Hold on her hands after the last word.
beats.narration: I'm moving more of my first finger along and my third and fourth finger are not moving as far so they just consequentially get closer to my first finger but actually my first finger is leading majority of the movement.
